title: Find the trace level of every handler the agent should trace

blocks.text: The tracing agent decides per handler class how closely to trace it, from a `@Traced(level = ...)` annotation. Teams put it where it suits them: on the handler class, on a base class their handlers extend, or on a service interface such as `Ingest`, which a handler may implement directly, through its base class, or through another interface (`interface BulkIngest extends Ingest`). After the last release the agent's dashboards show no traces from about a third of the handlers, all of them handlers that teams say are annotated.

Finish `levelOf(Class<?> handler)` and `fromInterfaces(Class<?>[] interfaces)` in `src/main/java/practice/TraceLookup.java`. A handler is traced at the level of the `@Traced` on its class or nearest superclass; failing that, at the level of the first traced interface found from the class upward; with none anywhere, it isn't traced. About twelve lines in total.

cases.says: a handler class that carries @Traced itself is traced at its own level, default or written
a handler with @Traced on no class and no interface of its hierarchy is not traced
a handler that implements a traced interface is traced at the interface's level
a handler whose superclass is traced is traced at that level, which wins over an interface's
a traced interface counts when a superclass implements it or another interface extends it

origin.section: @Inherited Reaches a Class Only from Its Superclasses

concepts: @Inherited makes getAnnotation find a class annotation on the nearest superclass, never on an interface, a method or for an annotation without @Inherited.
